hypothesis: During human growth, body weight scales approximately with the cube of linear stature, so the log-log slope of weight on stature across ages is about 3, and stature cubed reproduces most of the shape of the weight-by-age curve but not all of it.
pass_criterion: Use NHANES measured children and adolescents aged 2-19 y, with sex-specific medians for each single year of age, pooled over survey cycles with exam weights. Regress ln(median weight kg) on ln(median standing height cm) separately for boys and girls. PASS if both sex-specific slopes lie between 2.6 and 3.4, and the 95% bootstrap CI of each slope (resampling PSU/strata) overlaps 3.0. In addition, scaling the stature curve as (H/H_age2)^3 * W_age2 must reproduce the median weight-for-age curve with R^2 >= 0.90, and the residual (observed minus cubic-predicted weight) must be systematically non-zero. Specifically, the mean absolute residual must be >= 3% of weight, so the cube explains the curve 'mainly though not wholly'.
fail_criterion: FAIL if either sex-specific slope is below 2.5 or above 3.5, or if the 95% bootstrap CI excludes the whole 2.6-3.4 range, or if R^2 of the cubic-predicted weight curve against observed median weight is below 0.90. Results that fall between these bounds are inconclusive and not counted as a pass.
interpretation: Thompson's 'linear dimension' is measured standing height (stature). 'Weight' is measured body mass, assuming roughly constant density, so weight tracks volume. 'Tends to vary as the cube' is read as a log-log allometric exponent near 3 across the growth period, tested on age-wise medians. 'Mainly though not wholly' is operationalised as high R^2 of the cubic prediction together with a small but non-zero systematic residual, expected from changing body proportions and composition (e.g. adolescent BMI rise). Under 2 y, recumbent length is used in NHANES rather than standing height, so the test is restricted to ages 2-19 to keep the stature measure consistent. Modern reinterpretation: the exponent is estimated across ages with population medians, not within individual longitudinal growth trajectories.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) - Body Measures (BMX) examination data
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS)
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES records measured, not self-reported, standing height and body weight for a nationally representative sample across all ages and both sexes. Fields used: BMXWT (weight, kg), BMXHT (standing height, cm), RIDAGEYR (age in years), RIAGENDR (sex), and the exam weights WTMEC2YR with SDMVPSU and SDMVSTRA from the demographics file. Files are downloadable as SAS XPT for each cycle.
